the class 2 DHODs from E. coli and human are structurally different from the class 1 DHDOs from yeast and E. coli, and the structural differences explain why the two classes of enzyme have different inhibitors.
class 2 dihydroorotate-dehydrogenases (EC 1.3.3.1) are structurally and functionally distinct from class 1 enzymes.

the elucidation of the structure of class 1 and 2 dihydroorotate (DHO) dehydrogenases from different organisms.
the elucidation of the molecular basis of the catalytic mechanism of DHODs and the design of inhibitors of the enzymes.
the structural characterization of enzymes of the de novo biosynthetic pathway for pyrimidines.

the class 2 enzymes are more complex than the class 1 DHs, and that the differences between these two classes are not limited to the catalytic site.
